title: The AI Boom and the Future of Finance
gist: A short framing note arguing that the $27 trillion of market value added by AI-related companies since November 2022 rests on circular, increasingly debt-financed investment against still-speculative revenues — but that a bursting bubble would not end the underlying AI transformation.

insights.claim: AI-related companies have gained some $27 trillion in market value since November 2022.
insights.speaker: PS EDITORS
insights.so_what: Sizes the drawdown at risk if AI multiples compress — a shock of that scale is an index-level, not sector-level, event.
insights.quote: AI-related companies have gained some $27 trillion in market value since November 2022

insights.claim: AI investment has been largely circular and increasingly debt-financed while the revenues underwriting it remain highly speculative.
insights.speaker: PS EDITORS
insights.so_what: The fragility sits in credit, not just equity — watch AI-linked debt issuance and vendor-financing structures as the transmission channel.
insights.quote: investments have been largely circular and increasingly debt-financed, whereas revenues still highly speculative

insights.claim: A collapse in AI valuations would cause enormous economic pain but would not spell the end of the AI-driven transformation already underway.
insights.speaker: PS EDITORS
insights.so_what: Separates the financial cycle from the adoption cycle — a valuation crash is a buying setup for durable AI infrastructure rather than a thesis-killer.
insights.quote: while a collapse would cause enormous economic pain, no one should assume that it would spell the end of the AI-driven transformation currently underway
insights.locator: But while a collapse would cause

insights.claim: Public sentiment has shifted far enough against AI — over mass layoffs, destruction of books, sweeping copyright violations and data-center environmental damage — that an increasingly popular refrain is that the AI bubble cannot burst soon enough.
insights.speaker: PS EDITORS
insights.so_what: Hostile public opinion raises the probability of regulatory and litigation drag on AI buildouts independent of the financial cycle.
insights.quote: an increasingly popular refrain is that the AI bubble cannot burst soon enough
